result.keywords: This article proposes a mediation model examining how knowledge sharing and service resilience influence the relationship between participative leadership and staff performance in public libraries in Ghana. A quantitative design grounded in a positivist approach was used. Questionnaire data were collected from 248 library staff working in university and public libraries, and the data were analysed using factor analysis and multiple regression techniques. The findings indicate that knowledge sharing partially mediates the relationship between participative leadership and staff performance, while service resilience shows a stronger indirect effect in libraries facing budgetary and staffing constraints. The study contributes to library management research by linking leadership, internal knowledge processes, and performance outcomes in a sub-Saharan African public service context.
result.title: Knowledge sharing and service resilience as mediators in the relationship between participative leadership and staff performance in public libraries in Ghana.
